feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Tree-Ising: Repairing Language Models with Bit-Level Ising Edits
entry.summary:
Tree-Ising repairs language model reasoning loops by casting BF16 weight edits into sparse discrete QUBO/Ising problems, outperforming LLM-agent weight repairs while consuming zero tokens and fewer weight edits.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that discrete, training-free model edits can be solved deterministically and cheaply via Ising optimization, providing a more resource-efficient alternative to LLM-agent weight-space programming.

entry.title: World In-Context Learning for Agentic Robot Manipulation
entry.summary:
RoboScript introduces World In-Context Learning (WICL), enabling frozen foundation models to learn robot manipulation tasks from a single demonstration via simulation rehearsal and context updating without updating network weights.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that frozen foundation models can outperform specialized end-to-end trained policies in robotic manipulation by relying entirely on in-context memory built through simulated rehearsal.

entry.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
WikiTrace introduces an evidence-linked memory system for LLM agents that links concise lessons back to trajectory summaries and raw execution logs to mitigate memory-induced degradation.

Why it matters: By providing a mechanism for agents to ground and verify generated lessons against original execution logs, WikiTrace makes long-term agentic memory systems significantly more reliable.

entry.title: Few-Step Streaming Video Generation via Condition Shifting
entry.summary:
APEX extends streaming video generation to few-step sampling by using condition shifting to eliminate independent fake-score networks, reducing GPU memory and iteration time while improving instruction following and visual aesthetics.

Why it matters: By removing the separate fake-score network in streaming video distillation, APEX lowers training compute and memory overhead while maintaining high instruction adherence and visual quality over long 180-second video generations.

entry.title: dNaViT: Discrete Codes are General-Purpose Visual Representations
entry.summary:
dNaViT is a Discrete Native-resolution Vision Transformer that uses residual modulation and grouped product quantization to convert images into a compact, discrete visual vocabulary suitable for both vision understanding and image generation.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that a single compact discrete token vocabulary can unify visual understanding, generation, and editing within the same native autoregressive framework used by language models.

entry.title: MMDM: Measuring Massive Multitask Decision Making
entry.summary:
MMDM is a new benchmark featuring 5,448 questions across 16 categories designed to evaluate non-autoregressive System-1 decision models on complex, long-context, and constraint-heavy tasks.

Why it matters: It reveals critical limitations in current non-autoregressive decision models regarding joint reasoning, constraint satisfaction, and multi-select tasks in long-context environments.

entry.title: Infrathon: Benchmarking Language Agents for Real-World, Long-Horizon AI Infra Optimization
entry.summary:
Infrathon is a benchmark that evaluates frontier AI agents on long-horizon infrastructure optimization tasks over 24-hour evaluation budgets.

Why it matters: Short-horizon benchmarks misrepresent true model rankings and miss optimization gains that only emerge when agents run over extended timeframes.

entry.title: FINCOSMOS: An Open-World Evaluation Paradigm for Agents in Finance
entry.summary:
FINCOSMOS is an open-world evaluation paradigm for financial agents that tests Web data retrieval, strategy generation, and backtesting without reference answers using programmatic verification and veto checks.

Why it matters: It reveals that current LLM agents fail completely in realistic, open-world financial tasks due to silent errors like data leakage and unverified strategies, while proving memory-based feedback can remediate these failures.

entry.title: WaveGen: Truly End-to-End Waveform Generation via Internal Spectral Trajectory Learning
entry.summary:
WaveGen introduces Spectral Forcing, a diffusion-based framework that generates text-to-waveform audio end-to-end without external codecs, vocoders, duration predictors, or self-supervised text/audio embeddings.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that competitive text-to-speech models can be trained in a single stage from scratch without relying on complex, multi-module pipelines or pretrained external feature extractors.

entry.title: MotionGraphicsBench: Evaluating Motion Graphics Generation with Programmatic Verification
entry.summary:
MotionGraphicsBench is an expert-curated benchmark of 100 SVG animation instances evaluated using deterministic, human-readable verification programs instead of VLM judges or reference animation comparisons.

Why it matters: It isolates motion generation from graphic generation, offering an objective, code-based verification method that outperforms VLM judges for evaluating complex spatio-temporal LLM outputs.

entry.title: ProTEUS: A mutation-resolved world model for closed-loop protein evolution
entry.summary:
ProTEUS is a mutation-resolved world model that combines a mutation-biased attention architecture with fast physics-constrained structural prediction for closed-loop, multi-objective protein evolution.

Why it matters: It enables rapid, computationally efficient traversal of complex protein fitness landscapes to design variants with significantly higher functional activity using minimal experimental rounds.

entry.title: PhysOPSD: Code as Privilege for Physically Plausible Video Generation
entry.summary:
PhysOPSD uses executable code from a simulation engine as privileged physical context within an On-Policy Self-Distillation framework to generate physically plausible videos.

Why it matters: It enables video generative models to adhere to physical laws and complex interactions using a lightweight dataset of programmatically controlled simulations.

entry.title: The Surprising Effectiveness of Deleting Weights in LLM Post-Training
entry.summary:
Deletion Tuning acquires new LLM capabilities by zeroing under 0.05% of pretrained weights via a binary mask on gate projections, matching full fine-tuning performance without altering unmasked weights.

Why it matters: This method drastically reduces post-training checkpoint sizes by hundreds to thousands of times compared to FFT while preserving base-model performance on prior tasks.

entry.title: e-means: outperforming k-means (in one-tenth the epochs)
entry.summary:
e-means optimizes mini-batch k-means using exponential moving average updates, matching or beating Lloyd's k-means loss in one-tenth the epochs.

Why it matters: e-means enables order-of-magnitude faster, scalable clustering for massive embedding datasets, drastically cutting GPU compute costs for quantization, retrieval, and data curation.

entry.title: ExRL: Sample-Efficient Online Adaptation of Long-Chunk Policies via Execution Length Control
entry.summary:
ExRL achieves sample-efficient online policy adaptation by shifting RL optimization from high-dimensional action chunk vectors to a lightweight adapter that predicts execution length per chunk.

Why it matters: It enables practical, real-world fine-tuning of pre-trained long-chunk robot policies using minimal physical interaction data.

entry.title: Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents
entry.summary:
WikiTrace introduces an evidence-linked memory system that reduces LLM agent degradation by connecting concise lessons to trajectory summaries and raw execution logs for on-demand verification.

Why it matters: Linking distilled agent memories directly to verifiable execution traces prevents performance regression caused by faulty, ambiguous, or misapplied past lessons.

entry.title: A Theory of Policy Optimization in Post-Training: Coverage Collapse and Reference Resets
entry.summary:
This paper identifies coverage collapse in REINFORCE-based methods like PPO and GRPO and proves that Approximate Policy Mirror Descent with periodic reference resets prevents it, establishing global convergence guarantees governed by base model coverage.

Why it matters: It provides theoretical proof that resetting KL reference models prevents optimization stalls, giving practitioners principled guidelines for designing sample-efficient post-training RL algorithms.

entry.title: Stagewise and interpretable emergence of inside-outside computation in Transformer-based language models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that Transformers learn inside-outside parsing algorithms on context-free grammars in interpretable, analytically calculable stages, developing a distinct encoder-decoder depth structure during training.

Why it matters: Analytically mapping the stagewise training dynamics of parsing algorithms provides a theoretical foundation for understanding how modern LLMs resolve syntactic ambiguity.

entry.title: Beyond Passive Imitation: On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation for Language Models
entry.summary:
On-Policy Mid-Training Distillation (OPMD) replaces next-token prediction in continual pre-training by sampling student trajectories at anchor positions and optimizing them using dense token-level reverse-KL rewards from a frozen teacher.

Why it matters: It provides a model-aware alternative to passive domain adaptation that mitigates training-generation mismatch and prevents performance degradation during continual pre-training.

entry.title: POEM: Output-Relative Block-Sparse Attention for Long-Context Prefilling
entry.summary:
Target-free Entropy-guided Residual Modulation (TERM) is an inference-time defense that adaptively modulates an LLM's residual updates using prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations to mitigate jailbreaks without predefined safety directions.

Why it matters: It improves jailbreak resistance while limiting over-refusal on benign requests and avoiding the need for static, pre-trained safety vectors.

entry.title: TERM: Target-Free Jailbreak Defense via Entropy-Guided Residual Modulation
entry.summary:
TERM is an inference-time LLM jailbreak defense that dynamically modulates residual updates using prompt-calibrated attention entropy deviations, eliminating the need for predefined safety target directions.

Why it matters: It provides a low-overhead, inference-time safeguard against jailbreaks while reducing over-refusal on benign requests without requiring manual target tuning or offline steering vector extraction.

entry.title: Precision on Demand: Escalating Weight Bits at Uncertain Decoding Steps in a Small Local Model
entry.summary:
A dynamic quantization strategy for Qwen3-0.6B on GSM8K decodes primarily using 4-bit weights and re-executes steps at 8-bit precision only when output entropy or top-two margin thresholds signal token uncertainty.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that selective, step-wise weight precision escalation based on output uncertainty can recover near-full-precision accuracy while reducing total memory bandwidth consumption during local LLM inference.

entry.title: Blurring the Block Boundaries: Overlapping Block Denoising for Efficient Diffusion Language Models
entry.summary:
Blurring the Block Boundaries (B3) accelerates self-editing block Diffusion Language Models by up to 14.5% by dynamically refining adjacent token blocks in parallel within a shared forward pass.

Why it matters: B3 advances the Pareto frontier for inference latency in diffusion language models, making non-autoregressive generation faster without retraining or adding hyperparameter tuning overhead.

entry.title: Forward-Value Discretization: Faster Stochastic Diffusion Sampling Without High-Order Approximation
entry.summary:
Forward-value discretization introduces training-free lookahead prediction models (F-DDPM and F-DPMSolver) that improve stochastic diffusion sampling efficiency without requiring higher-order approximations.

Why it matters: It enables faster, higher-quality stochastic diffusion sampling without retraining or relying on complex high-order mathematical approximations.

entry.title: When Should Agents Remember? Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution for LLM Agents
entry.summary:
Falsification-Gated Self-Evolution (FGSE) introduces a framework that treats LLM agent memory updates as structured hypotheses, validating them via transfer, falsification, and regression probes before committing them to persistent state.

Why it matters: It prevents local episode successes from inserting unverified or unsafe knowledge into an agent's long-term memory, ensuring safer and more reliable self-improvement.

entry.title: Learning Heterogeneous Tactile Representation for General Dexterous Manipulation
entry.summary:
LingBot-Touch is a tactile foundation model that unifies heterogeneous sensor data into a plug-and-play representation to enhance general dexterous manipulation across diverse policy architectures.

Why it matters: It enables embodied AI models to scale tactile learning by leveraging cross-sensor data despite heterogeneous hardware physics.

entry.title: WorldFoundry: Towards Unified Infrastructure for World Intelligence
entry.summary:
WorldFoundry is an open-source infrastructure designed for reproducible inference and evaluation of generative world models across video, 3D/4D, embodied action, and interactive systems.

Why it matters: It enables unified, reproducible evaluation of persistent and controllable physical dynamics across highly heterogeneous visual and embodied AI systems.

entry.title: Toward the Era of Agentic Embodied Intelligence
entry.summary:
A2-MEAS is an embodied multi-agent framework that uses learned correction codes and the A2-WLA action model to improve robotic task performance and real-time failure recovery.

Why it matters: The framework significantly increases robot failure-recovery rates and task completion while operating at 4.03x the training throughput of existing baselines like pi0.5.

entry.title: Sage-Taiyi: A Metacognitive Architecture for Scientific Discovery
entry.summary:
Sage-Taiyi is a metacognitive AI architecture that uses explicit monitoring and control of scientific understanding to adapt research targets and select reusable reasoning methods for automated scientific discovery.

Why it matters: Demonstrates that metacognitive self-regulation enables AI systems to generate validated scientific ideations and directly improve real-world physical and chemical experiment yields.

entry.title: PCBRouteAgent: How Close Are LLM Agents to Becoming PCB Routing Engineers?
entry.summary:
PCBRouteAgent is a multimodal LLM agent that automates PCB routing by combining a Global Routing Planner with KiCad's native execution engine and bounded local recovery.

Why it matters: It demonstrates how LLM agents can orchestrate native EDA tools to bridge high-level strategy and low-level geometric routing in hardware design.

entry.title: Reframe: Observation-Aligned Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation for Agentic Visual Reasoning
entry.summary:
Reframe is a post-training framework for visual agents that aligns observation states using Ground-Drop-GRPO and Observation-Gated Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation without requiring a task-specific SFT cold start.

Why it matters: By aligning observation states and repairing faulty tool interactions mid-rollout, Reframe improves visual reasoning performance without needing task-specific supervised fine-tuning.

entry.title: ReproBridge: Building Reproducibility into ML Research Artifacts
entry.summary:
ReproBridge is an agent workflow that creates standardized reproducible ML artifacts to boost downstream coding agent reproduction success.

Why it matters: Preserving execution details and refined code enables diverse AI models to reproduce research experiments far more reliably and at a lower compute cost.

entry.title: Longtail-SWE: High-Quality SWE Tasks for Underrepresented Languages
entry.summary:
Longtail-SWE is a new benchmark featuring 202 repository-level issue-resolution tasks across 13 underrepresented programming languages, built using a solver-judge-repairer pipeline to fix defective tests and ambiguous task descriptions.

Why it matters: It expands software engineering agent evaluations beyond mainstream ecosystems like Python or JavaScript into 13 long-tail languages using higher-quality, repaired issue benchmarks.

entry.title: SIRIS: Can LLMs Tell When Simulation Errors Matter in AI-Driven Systems Research
entry.summary:
Siris is a novel benchmark that evaluates whether LLMs can determine if simulator errors and modeling limitations invalidate design recommendations in AI-driven systems research.

Why it matters: As LLM agents increasingly automate systems research using imperfect simulators, models must accurately discern when simulation inaccuracies truly impact real-world design decisions.

entry.title: How Much Training-Inference Mismatch Can On-Policy Distillation Tolerate?
entry.summary:
A study on on-policy distillation (OPD) demonstrates its resilience to training-inference mismatch from quantization and asynchronous rollouts, enabling faster FP8 training via a lightweight admission check.

Why it matters: The findings allow practitioners to aggressively optimize OPD training speed and memory efficiency using FP8 and asynchronous rollouts without sacrificing model performance or risking RL instability.

entry.title: InfraRSI: Harnessing Recursive Self-Improvement for Training Infrastructure
entry.summary:
InfraRSI is an agentic harness that applies a five-stage recursive self-improvement workflow to co-optimize LLM training launch settings, operator kernels, and communication schedules.

Why it matters: It enables automated, end-to-end optimization of distributed LLM training infrastructure while safely managing memory boundaries, hardware noise, and cross-GPU experience transfer.

entry.title: Steerable Multi-Objective Group-Relative Preference Optimization with Jointly Trained Low-Rank Adapters
entry.summary:
LambdaMix introduces a parameter-efficient method that jointly trains one low-rank adapter per objective using group-relative online reinforcement learning to enable real-time, preference-steerable policy selection from a single training run.

Why it matters: It enables language models to adapt dynamically to shifting user preference trade-offs at inference time using a single set of lightweight adapters, reducing both compute and storage costs.

entry.title: CPU-ARC: Agentic Reasoning Caching for on-CPU Reasoning Reuse
entry.summary:
CPU-ARC extracts robust, CPU-executable agentic reasoning caches from LLM reasoning traces, decoupling task-solving logic from model execution.

Why it matters: It enables low-cost, explainable, and energy-efficient deployment of complex reasoning workflows on standard CPUs without relying on expensive LLM inference for every task instance.

entry.title: Training Vision Transformers to Focus: Emergence of Spatial Attention Head Specialization
entry.summary:
A novel training method uses two visual focusing loss functions to induce spatial attention head specialization in self-supervised Vision Transformers without requiring annotations.

Why it matters: It improves the spatial precision and interpretability of self-supervised Vision Transformers, enhancing downstream dense prediction tasks like zero-shot segmentation without adding manual labeling overhead.

entry.title: FewStepRL: Fine-tuning Few-step Diffusion Models with Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
FewStepRL adapts RL objectives to few-step diffusion models via a three-phase framework comprising transformation, decomposition, and adaptation.

Why it matters: It removes the heavy computational bottleneck of rolling out many-step diffusion samplers during RL post-training while unifying diverse RL objectives into a single modular framework.

entry.title: Interpretability Is Not Model-Specific
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that interpretability tools like refusal vectors and sentiment probes can be transferred across different language models using linear maps fit purely on unlabeled prompts.

Why it matters: Interpretability tools like steering vectors and diagnostic probes can be reused across different AI models by fitting a map with a few unlabeled prompts, avoiding the expense of re-extracting them from scratch.

entry.title: DForkTree: Accelerating Speculative Decoding with Fork-Aware Block Diffusion Draft Trees
entry.summary:
DForkTree is a training-free speculative decoding method that improves block diffusion draft tree accuracy by re-anchoring branches using local n-gram statistics and exact GPU tree construction.

Why it matters: It improves LLM inference speed over existing speculative decoding tree methods without requiring additional model training or architecture modifications.

entry.title: What the Loss Curve Misses: FP4 Pretraining Slows the Acquisition of Rare Facts
entry.summary:
Pretraining transformers with 4-bit floating-point (NVFP4) matrix multiplications requires up to 1.52x more exposures than BF16 to learn rare facts, despite showing minimal validation loss differences.

Why it matters: Evaluating low-precision quantization recipes solely on validation loss masks a significant drop in a model's efficiency at acquiring rare factual knowledge.

entry.title: A Geometric Invariant of Attention Predicts Head Specialization from Weights Alone
entry.summary:
Researchers derived a scalar invariant, ρ, that predicts transformer head specialization—such as induction heads—directly from weight matrices without executing forward passes.

Why it matters: It enables data-independent, zero-cost analysis and targeted context-extension fine-tuning of transformer heads directly from weight matrices.

entry.title: Lost in Rounding: bf16 Recurrent State Makes Hybrid Reasoning Models Think Longer
entry.summary:
Storing recurrent states in bfloat16 with round-to-nearest causes hybrid reasoning models to generate longer outputs and degrade accuracy, a issue resolved using stochastic rounding.

Why it matters: Serving hybrid reasoning models with standard bfloat16 RTN state caching severely degrades speed and accuracy, requiring stochastic rounding or explicit state-dtype reporting to ensure valid evaluations.

entry.title: Translating KV Caches Between Hybrid-Attention Language Models: MLA Latents, Linear-Attention States and Sparse-Attention Indexers
entry.summary:
Researchers developed methods to translate KV caches between hybrid-attention language models, enabling context hand-offs across MLA latents, linear-attention states, and sparse-attention indexers without re-reading prompt histories.

Why it matters: KV-cache translation drastically cuts latency and computational costs when handing off long-context conversations between non-identical, modern hybrid-attention models without requiring full prefill re-computation.

entry.title: When Answer Decodability Is Not a Decision: Separating Final-Answer and Imminent-Emission Signals in Chain-of-Thought
entry.summary:
Researchers developed Emission-Controlled Dual-Target Probing (ECDP) to prove that strong chain-of-thought answer decodability often reflects imminent token emission rather than an early, finalized model decision.

Why it matters: Probing high answer-candidate decodability in hidden states cannot automatically be interpreted as a finalized model decision without controlling for imminent text emission.

entry.title: HiVe-Mem: Interleaving Horizontal Memory Expansion and Vertical Evidence Composition for Multimodal Agents
entry.summary:
HiVe-Mem introduces a multimodal memory framework combining graph-based horizontal expansion with trainable vertical evidence composition to improve memory retrieval and evidence selection for long-term agent interactions.

Why it matters: It enables multimodal agents to maintain broader long-term memory context while drastically reducing context-window token overhead through adaptive evidence selection.

entry.title: Shortcuts and Boundaries: Verifiable RL Misalignment and Contextual Safety Learning
entry.summary:
A framework encodes verifiable reward-context conflicts into task dynamics to study RL misalignment, showing minority shortcut exposure induces high violation rates while simple binary execution penalties improve capability and compliance across changing workflows.

Why it matters: Verifiable context checks allow scalable training of RL agents that maintain compliance and adapt safety behaviors even as execution rules and authorization levels evolve.

entry.title: MaxIM: Maximally Informative Incremental Summarization via Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
MaxIM introduces a capacity-constrained, information-theoretic reward-shaping framework for reinforcement learning that optimizes incremental summarization to maintain bounded memory over long-horizon interaction histories without human preference labels.

Why it matters: It enables LLMs to maintain accurate, bounded memory over unbounded context lengths for complex tasks without relying on expensive human annotations.

entry.title: SplatAnything: Gaussian Spacing Normalization for Feed-forward 3DGS across Arbitrary Scenes
entry.summary:
SplatAnything introduces Gaussian Spacing Normalization (GSNorm) to canonicalize scene-level Gaussian center spacing, resolving scale mismatches and improving feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting across diverse scene scales and camera configurations.

Why it matters: By standardizing Gaussian spatial metrics, the method enables robust, scale-invariant feed-forward 3D reconstruction across arbitrary and unconstrained camera setups.

entry.title: P^2-MOPD: Accelerating Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation via Parameter Priors
entry.summary:
P^2-MOPD accelerates multi-teacher on-policy distillation by treating expert parameters as differentiable priors while keeping student weights trainable, reaching target performance in half the training steps.

Why it matters: This approach significantly reduces the compute time required to distill multiple expert models into a single student LLM while achieving superior final capability recovery.

entry.title: LowRAM: Low-Rank Keys and Amortised Values for Composable KV Cache Compression at Test-Time
entry.summary:
LowRAM introduces asymmetric KV cache compression by combining cross-layer low-rank key compression with value cache amortisation, fitting per-head value predictors from keys at test time to achieve high compression with minimal decoding overhead.

Why it matters: Treating keys and values as structurally distinct allows substantial reductions in KV cache memory footprint, directly scaling decode throughput and batch sizes for long-context LLM inference.

entry.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
entry.summary:
The HEELO framework introduces agent-native primitives—reusable resource units powered by resident LLMs—to bridge execution failures between reaching and applying resources in real-world agent tasks.

Why it matters: Encapsulating resource competence within agent-native primitives eliminates redundant harness development while significantly increasing task success rates, execution speed, and cost efficiency for frontier models.

entry.title: LongBanana: An Expert-Verified Benchmark for Long-Context Multi-Reference Image Synthesis
entry.summary:
LongBanana is an expert-verified benchmark and graph-grounded evaluation framework for long-context multi-reference image synthesis, accompanied by LongBanana-Gen, an agent-harness baseline.

Why it matters: It establishes a standardized, auditable metric for evaluating how multi-modal agent systems retrieve, bind, and synthesize dense visual evidence from large sets of reference images.

entry.title: Beneath the Surface: What We Overlook When We Talk About Agent Evolution
entry.summary:
A study on agent harness evolution shows that benchmark score gains mask task coverage loss, increased deployment costs, and inconsistent transferability, prompting the creation of the improved EvoAudit framework.

Why it matters: Evaluating self-improving agent harnesses solely on aggregate benchmark scores can hide regressions, rising inference costs, and poor transferability across different domains.

entry.title: EvoWorld: Towards Out-of-Sight World Evolution in Generative Video Models
entry.summary:
EvoWorld introduces a brain-renderer framework that combines a vision-language model for state reasoning with a segment-autoregressive video renderer to enable out-of-sight causal world evolution.

Why it matters: It addresses the limitation of current diffusion video models by introducing explicit state reasoning, allowing visual world simulators to generate causally consistent and behaviorally reactive video environments.

entry.title: Video-Coder: Reinforcing Agentic Coding for Video Generation
entry.summary:
Video-Coder is a code-driven video generation agent that writes and executes code to render dynamic 3D draft videos, providing explicit structural and motion guidance to downstream video generators.

Why it matters: By leveraging executable code to build 3D draft scenes, Video-Coder significantly improves spatial structure, motion coherence, and scene control in generated videos.

entry.title: Confucius4-R2T2: A Stable-Prefix Streaming ASR Model for Real Real-Time Transcription
entry.summary:
Confucius4-R2T2 introduces a stable-prefix streaming ASR method using Longest Stable Prefix (LSP) post-training to eliminate output revisions without altering model architecture.

Why it matters: It prevents downstream systems like voice agents and machine translators from wasting compute or taking erroneous actions caused by revised streaming tokens.

entry.title: AutoCompress: Automated Hardware-Guided Model Compression
entry.summary:
AutoCompress is a hardware-guided compression framework using differentiable architecture search to directly optimize LLM pruning against serving-engine cost models for specific latency, throughput, and memory constraints.

Why it matters: It eliminates manual trial-and-error model size selection by automating LLM compression directly against actual deployment hardware and serving engine metrics.

entry.title: Exploring Weight-Space Programming: Capabilities, Generalization, and Limitations
entry.summary:
Systematic evaluation of Weight-Space Programming across seven benchmarks reveals that reasoning agents modifying neural parameters directly can achieve large accuracy gains with localized edits, but suffer from inconsistent intervention discovery.

Why it matters: Weight-Space Programming offers a parameter-efficient alternative to gradient-based fine-tuning, though reliable edit discovery remains a key bottleneck.

entry.title: Frontier3DBench: Benchmarking Coding Agents for 3D Creation across Objects, Scenes, and Interactive Open Worlds
entry.summary:
Frontier3DBench is a new benchmark evaluating coding agents for 3D creation across 145 tasks in object, scene, and interactive open-world levels.

Why it matters: The benchmark identifies reference fidelity and coordinated stateful activity completion as the critical failure modes for LLM-driven 3D generation agents.

entry.title: LLMs Don't Know What They Know: Benchmarking Temporal Self-Knowledge for Financial Backtesting
entry.summary:
The FinDendro benchmark reveals that frontier LLMs understate their temporal knowledge via self-reports, invalidating common safeguards used to prevent data leakage in financial backtesting.

Why it matters: Financial backtests cannot rely on stated cutoffs, self-reporting, or date-prompting to prevent lookahead bias, necessitating behavioral benchmarks to verify true knowledge boundaries.

entry.title: Authorization Drift in LLM Agents: Evaluating Boundary Compliance in Multi-Step Tool Use
entry.summary:
Researchers formalized non-adversarial authorization drift in LLM agents and introduced the Authorization Drift Benchmark (ADB) using Staged Execution-Reflective Synthesis (SERS) to evaluate boundary compliance across multi-step tool use.

Why it matters: As LLM agents gain operational autonomy, their tendency to bypass permission boundaries for efficiency exposes deployment environments to severe privacy and data protection non-compliance.

entry.title: OmniLatent: Unified Latent for 3D Part Modeling
entry.summary:
OmniLatent presents a unified 3D part modeling framework that jointly encodes geometry, deformation, appearance, and binary part IDs into a single shared latent space for single-image part-aware asset generation.

Why it matters: It enables direct generation of editable, part-decomposed 3D assets from single images while avoiding post-processing segmentation artifacts and enabling precise interactive editing.

entry.title: On the Reliability of Majority-Vote Pseudo-Labels in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Researchers introduce Prompt-Conditional Distributionally Robust DPO (PC-Dr.DPO) and a cache mechanism to mitigate finite-rollout variation and self-supervised forgetting during test-time reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: It improves the stability and performance of language model test-time adaptation on unlabeled target domains without requiring external supervision.

entry.title: ENGRAM: From Agent Experience to Weights through Verified Consolidation
entry.summary:
ENGRAM decouples agent training admission from memory release, using demonstration-aware gating and probe-based verification to safely consolidate retrieval-based experiences into model weights.

Why it matters: It minimizes the external retrievable memory footprint, input-token usage, and model calls while maintaining agent performance close to retain-all retrieval baselines.

entry.title: From LoRA to Language: Recovering Skill Documents from Adapters
entry.summary:
Researchers developed methods to reverse-engineer textual skill documents from LoRA adapters and frozen base models, successfully recovering up to 44% of key instructions and restoring up to 91% of original task gains.

Why it matters: Decompiling opaque LoRA weights back into human-readable skill documents enables auditing, editing, and transferring adapter capabilities across non-compatible model architectures.

entry.title: Not All Entropy Is Equal: Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
entry.summary:
Reward-Conditioned Entropy Allocation (RCEA) is a new diagnostic framework that separates trajectory-level and token-level entropy by verifier outcome, demonstrating that global policy entropy does not reliably track reasoning performance in RLVR.

Why it matters: Evaluating policy collapse in RLVR requires analyzing which specific uncertainty is removed via reward-stratified metrics rather than relying on global token entropy.

entry.title: Logit Laundering: Evading Data-Use Auditing in Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Logit Laundering is a novel inference-time evasion framework that manipulates LLM output logits to suppress data-watermarking signals, allowing non-compliant model providers to evade data-use auditing without altering model parameters.

Why it matters: It reveals a critical vulnerability in current LLM data-use auditing techniques, showing that unauthorized training on copyrighted data can be concealed at inference time.

entry.title: Designing Effective Monitor-Based Interventions for Mitigating Reward Hacking During RL
entry.summary:
Researchers open-sourced three RL environments where Qwen3-4B reward hacks, demonstrating how design choices in monitor-based interventions affect evasion, learning signal leakage, and mitigation across domains.

Why it matters: Understanding monitor design trade-offs prevents reinforcement learning models from learning to evade oversight mechanisms while suppressing unintended behaviors like hallucination and code manipulation.

entry.title: A Tight Hierarchy for Chain of Thought
entry.summary:
Researchers established the first strict hierarchy theorem for Chain of Thought reasoning, proving that increasing CoT steps from O(r(n)) to O(r(n)^(1+e)) strictly expands the computational power of transformers.

Why it matters: It theoretically proves that granting transformers more Chain of Thought reasoning steps strictly increases the class of decision problems the model can solve.

entry.title: RidgeFill: Training-Free Late-Layer Cache Fill for Faster Prefill
entry.summary:
RidgeFill is a training-free technique that accelerates prefill by using closed-form ridge regression to project lower-layer states into late-layer KV caches.

Why it matters: It enables immediate, training-free TTFT speedups on existing pre-trained LLMs by retrofitting late-layer KV cache filling via simple linear maps.

entry.title: Transformer-FSQ: Discrete Latents for Extreme KV-Cache Compression
entry.summary:
Transformer-FSQ achieves extreme KV-cache compression by replacing standard key and value projections with a finite scalar quantisation bottleneck, storing packed discrete integer vectors without per-token metadata.

Why it matters: It enables local consumer devices to retain significantly longer context windows by drastically reducing KV-cache memory footprints while maintaining attention throughput and accuracy.

entry.title: CodeQuant2: Enhanced Outlier Mitigation and Adaptive Clustering for Low-Precision LRMs
entry.summary:
CodeQuant2 is a clustering-based lookup table (LUT) quantization framework for low-precision large reasoning models that uses rotation, scaling, adaptive codebooks, and reasoning-aware calibration to improve accuracy and inference speed.

Why it matters: It restores accuracy in aggressively quantized large reasoning models while substantially reducing inference latency and compute costs.

entry.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
entry.summary:
Coca-Cola introduces a continuous latent context compression framework for LLM agents that compresses tool outputs into dense latent tokens instead of relying on discrete text tokens.

Why it matters: By bypassing discrete text summarization, agents can operate over significantly compressed context windows, decreasing latency and execution costs while enhancing decision-making accuracy.

entry.title: NPCBench: A Clinical Apprenticeship Benchmark for Multimodal Care-Pathway Reasoning in Nasopharyngeal Carcinoma
entry.summary:
NPCBench is a clinical apprenticeship benchmark for nasopharyngeal carcinoma that evaluates multimodal AI across longitudinal, integrated care pathways rather than isolated, static question-answering tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a realistic benchmark showing that current multimodal models struggle to maintain temporal coherence and jointly accurate reasoning across full clinical workflows.

entry.title: HERIT: Enabling Global Access to Hanja-to-English Historical Translation by Mitigating Temporal Bias
entry.summary:
HERIT is a domain-adaptation pipeline that uses retrieval-augmented generation to create high-quality Hanja-to-English pseudo-labeled data from Hanja-Korean corpora, reducing temporal bias and data scarcity in historical translation.

Why it matters: It provides a scalable machine translation pipeline to automatically make untranslated historical Hanja archives globally accessible to researchers without expensive manual effort.

entry.title: Embedding-Space Fingerprinting of LoRA Fine-Tunes: Recovering the Training-Data Domain from the Model Artifact Alone
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that a fine-tuned model's domain can be recovered from the artifact alone using black-box generated text or gray-box activations, outperforming white-box weight statistics.

Why it matters: LoRA fine-tunes leak training domain information through model outputs and activations, posing privacy and data-provenance risks even when direct weight access is restricted.

entry.title: The Gating Mechanism of KV Cache Eviction
entry.summary:
A learnable KV cache eviction gate trained inside the softmax using the dense model's predictions as a target prevents optimization from defaulting to a dense no-op.

Why it matters: It establishes the structural conditions required to successfully train learnable KV cache eviction mechanisms, enabling up to 75% compression with minimal loss in long-context accuracy.

entry.title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
entry.summary:
Researchers developed TraceMRT to red-team Chain-of-Thought monitors using contextual evasion strategies, exposing vulnerabilities in top LLM monitors and addressing them with a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring framework.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that current top-tier reasoning monitors can be bypassed by strategically concealed objectives, providing a more robust Bayesian detection method for autonomous agent safety.

entry.title: Learning the Task or Learning the Verifier? Rethinking Criteria Exposure in Embodied Self-Improvement
entry.summary:
Controlled experiments reveal that Criteria Exposure (CE) in embodied self-improvement causes coding agents to overfit to verification logic rather than learn robust, transferable task skills.

Why it matters: Exposing evaluation criteria to self-improving agents inflates benchmark scores through overfitting, requiring the adoption of instruction-faithful verifiers to measure genuine robot skill acquisition.

entry.title: Scaling Neural Motor Decoding via Decoupled Behavioral Pretraining
entry.summary:
BEEMO is a neural motor decoding framework that decouples behavioral and neural pretraining, enabling training on arbitrary mixtures of paired neural-behavioral recordings and unpaired behavioral trajectories to improve task transfer.

Why it matters: Scaling unpaired behavioral data provides a cost-effective pathway to build cross-subject and cross-task neural decoders without relying on invasive, expensive neural recordings.

entry.title: The Geometry of Simulated Perspectives: Dissociating Representation and Behaviour in a Multimodal Language Model
entry.summary:
A study on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct reveals a dissociation between internal representations and behavioral outputs, showing prompt framing impacts representational geometry more than persona identity, whereas persona content drives actual behavioral ratings.

Why it matters: Understanding the dissociation between internal representations and functional outputs is critical for interpreting how multimodal models process persona conditioning and for evaluating internal model states.

entry.title: Knowing When to Teach: Learning from Teachable Prefixes in Multilingual Reasoning Distillation
entry.summary:
Teachable On-Policy Self-Distillation (TOPSD) mitigates Teacher Drift in multilingual reasoning distillation by dynamically selecting verified, teachable prefix trajectories based on teacher-student likelihood.

Why it matters: TOPSD improves multilingual self-distillation efficiency and accuracy, particularly for lower-resource languages where intermediate reasoning mistakes typically cause standard distillation to fail.

entry.title: DictLLM: Post-training Compression of Large Language Model with Dictionary Kernels
entry.summary:
DictLLM introduces a post-training compression scheme that decomposes weight matrices across grouped layers into a single shared dictionary and layer-specific sparse coefficients, followed by quantization.

Why it matters: It enables significantly higher compression ratios for LLMs without requiring full retraining, facilitating memory-efficient deployment on mobile and edge devices.

entry.title: User Embeddings are Superpositions of Interpretable Behavioral Modes
entry.summary:
A post-hoc, model-agnostic framework applies sparse autoencoders (SAEs) to user embeddings to extract, interpret, and natural-language-label sparse superpositions of behavioral modes without modifying upstream models.

Why it matters: It provides a practical, post-hoc method to interpret, query, and operationalize opaque recommendation and personalization embeddings using natural language without retraining upstream models.

entry.title: Adversarial Training with Large Step Sizes: Implicit Bias, Optimization, and Sharpness
entry.summary:
This paper analyzes deterministic Gradient Descent with large constant step sizes in Adversarial Training, revealing fundamental dynamics that differ significantly from Standard Training and continuous-time flow approximations.

Why it matters: It bridges the gap between theoretical models using vanishing step sizes and practical adversarial training regimes using large constant step sizes.

entry.title: Module-Aware Optimization for Graph Neural Networks
entry.summary:
GraphMuon adapts the Muon optimizer to Graph Neural Networks by accounting for the covariance structure of graph-propagated layer inputs during matrix update orthogonalization.

Why it matters: GraphMuon significantly accelerates GNN training convergence without sacrificing predictive performance by aligning optimization updates with graph propagation dynamics.

entry.title: Discovering Learning Rules that Shape Others
entry.summary:
Discovered Update Rule for Opponent Shaping (DUOS) meta-learns an agent update rule for general-sum games that performs opponent shaping using only the agent's own experience, requiring no access to opponent parameters or policies.

Why it matters: It enables effective long-horizon opponent shaping and cooperation in general-sum games without requiring access to private opponent parameters or internal state.

entry.title: Beyond Quadratic Attention: Separable Gaussian Operators for ODE Vision Transformers
entry.summary:
SSoG replaces dense self-attention in Vision Transformers with learned, axis-factorized Gaussian kernels, achieving subquadratic complexity, global Lipschitz continuity, and lower parameter counts.

Why it matters: SSoG enables scalable, parameter-efficient processing of high-resolution images while providing formal mathematical stability guarantees for continuous-depth Neural ODE models.

entry.title: Multimodal-SEA: Benchmarking AI Agent Security under Multimodal Social Engineering Attacks
entry.summary:
Multimodal-SEA is a benchmark featuring 608 tasks across 152 scenarios to evaluate AI agent security against multimodal social engineering attacks.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that adding multimodal content significantly increases the vulnerability of personal AI agents to social engineering, highlighting limitations in current model safety alignment.

entry.title: From Twisted Facts to Rogue Agents: Can LLMs Reliably Detect Multi-Dimensional Hallucinations?
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced HaluCheck, a bilingual benchmark with over 42,000 instances designed to evaluate LLM hallucination detection, localization, and correction across factual text and agent trajectories.

Why it matters: It establishes a comprehensive benchmark for diagnosing fine-grained hallucination failure modes in both standard text generation and autonomous LLM agent execution.

entry.title: Do Recommenders Need to Think in Words? Latent Reasoning for Efficient LLM-Based Recommendation
entry.summary:
LatentRec introduces a framework that uses a 2.5M-parameter module to supervise intermediate latent reasoning steps during LLM recommendation training, allowing the module to be discarded at deployment for zero-token inference reasoning.

Why it matters: It eliminates the need to generate expensive chain-of-thought text or run latent modules during inference, shifting the computational cost of reasoning entirely to training time.

entry.title: Towards Foundation Decision Models: Drex
entry.summary:
Drex is an open-source family of four non-autoregressive decision models up to 37B parameters that directly output probability distributions over user-provided options.

Why it matters: Drex provides a lower-latency, cheaper, and order-stable alternative to autoregressive LLM reasoning for structured decision-making, classification, and scoring tasks.

entry.title: Decodability Is Not Validity: Evaluating Nuisance Sensitivity in Language Model Concept Probes
entry.summary:
A study shows that concept probe accuracy (AUROC) fails to reflect nuisance attribute sensitivity, but nuisance-aware development diagnostics can reduce counterfactual sensitivity with minimal accuracy loss.

Why it matters: High decoding accuracy alone is insufficient to validate concept probes, necessitating nuisance-aware evaluation to ensure probes measure the target concept rather than confounding variables.

entry.title: Extending Reasoning in Typed Decision Models via Looping
entry.summary:
RELOAD fine-tunes typed decision models by looping a middle layer block with a damped connection and a lightweight controller, enabling adaptive test-time compute in latent space to boost accuracy and calibration.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that non-generative decision models can scale test-time compute in latent space without parameter expansion, matching or beating the performance of much larger unrolled models.

entry.title: Continued Training of Continuous Language Flows with Token Identity Squared Supervision
entry.summary:
Token Identity Brier Flow (TIBF) improves continuous language flow models by using Brier loss squared supervision on token probabilities with frozen embeddings instead of standard continuous MSE.

Why it matters: TIBF resolves probability distribution ambiguity in continuous language flows, allowing pretrained models to achieve lower generative perplexity and fewer text repetitions under limited continued-training budgets.

entry.title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking
entry.summary:
SKIM is the first pruning and distillation framework designed specifically for LLM agents under structured generation, using token role partitioning to guide parameter pruning and distillation.

Why it matters: SKIM enables significantly smaller, highly compressed LLM agents to maintain accuracy during structured inference, such as tool-calling and grammar-constrained tasks.

entry.title: The Memory Trap: Language Agents Overgeneralize from Benign Interactions
entry.summary:
Evaluations across six frontier models reveal the 'memory trap,' where persistent memories from benign interactions cause agents to overgeneralize and exhibit unsafe or biased behavior in subsequent high-stakes tasks.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that harmless user interactions can inadvertently degrade safety, rigor, and alignment in later sessions highlights an urgent need for scope-aware agent memory systems.
